blocks.heading: The format
lines: Five jumbled sentences. Four make one paragraph; type the number of the one that doesn't fit.
Type-in answer, so a wrong answer costs nothing. Always type something.
Two in every CAT 2024 and 2025 paper. Give each about 3 minutes.

blocks.heading: The method
lines: Read all five once and write a three to five word gist of each.
Find links you can prove: a pronoun (this, they, such) and what it points to; a term defined in one sentence and used in another; "for example" after the claim it supports.
Build the chain of four from those links. The sentence left over is the answer.
Read the four in order once. If it flows without a gap, you're done.

blocks.heading: What usually makes a sentence the odd one
lines: Same topic, different focus: the paragraph is about causes and this sentence is about effects, or the paragraph is about one country and this sentence is about the world.
It needs a missing sentence to connect to the others.
A change of register: a personal story among general claims, or a statistic with nothing that leads to it.
It contradicts the chain's conclusion without being set up as a contrast.

blocks.heading: Traps
lines: Don't pick the sentence with the hardest words. The odd one is usually easy to read and on topic.
Don't drop a sentence because it starts with However or This. Find what it refers to first.
Two candidates: remove each in turn and read the other four. The right answer leaves no gap.
After 3 minutes, type your best candidate and move on.
